title: Merger or amalgamation of companies through the NCLT
law: Sections 230 and 232; Companies (Compromises, Arrangements and Amalgamations) Rules, 2016; for listed companies, Regulation 37 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015
summary: Combines two or more companies under a scheme that the NCLT sanctions after meetings, notices to authorities and hearings.
when: When companies want to merge or amalgamate and the fast-track route is not available or not chosen.
applies: Private and public companies; listed companies have extra steps (committees, stock exchange filings)

steps.d: Directors give in-principle approval to the merger. They pick the NCLT bench, authorise filing of the application, and appoint a registered valuer and other professionals (accountant, secretary in practice, consultants, lawyers). They also fix the date of the next board or shareholder meeting.

The Independent Directors Committee recommends the draft scheme and confirms it does not harm shareholders of the listed entity. The Audit Committee considers the valuation report and the share entitlement ratio and recommends the draft scheme. Its report covers need, rationale, synergies, impact on shareholders and cost-benefit.

Board approves the exchange ratio, the valuation report and the scheme. It authorises signatories and representatives, and approves filing the scheme copy with the ROC under section 232(2)(b). Listed companies also take the stock exchange in-principle approval, the merchant banker's fairness opinion and the Audit Committee recommendation, and choose a designated stock exchange with nationwide terminals. A public company files the board resolution with the ROC under sections 117(3)(g) and 179(3)(i).

Listed companies tell the stock exchange the board decision within 24 hours of the meeting. File MGT-14 within 30 days of the resolution. Submit the draft scheme and documents to the exchange under Regulation 37 and place the same on the company website.
docs: Pre and post merger shareholding of unlisted entity
Audited financials of last 3 years (not older than 6 months) of unlisted entity
Compliance report signed by CS, CFO and managing director

steps.d: Send the exchange a complaints report within 7 days after 21 days from filing the draft scheme. If any dues, fines or penalties are unpaid, send a report on unpaid dues together with the draft scheme, before the observation letter.

steps.t: First motion application to the NCLT
steps.d: File the application under section 230 with: consent affidavits of shareholders and creditors, a chartered accountant's certificate on creditors, and the auditor's certificate that the accounting treatment follows accounting standards (provisos to sections 230(7) and 232(3)). Draft the first motion application (NCLT-1), notice of admission (NCLT-2) and affidavit (NCLT-6). Ask for dispensation of a meeting where creditors holding 90% in value agree. Attach the creditors' responsibility statement (CAA-1).

The NCLT orders the meeting date, venue, chairman, the time for the chairman's report, and any dispensation for unlisted companies. File the order with the ROC within 30 days of receiving it. If no dispensation, send individual notices to shareholders and creditors, and publish the advertisement in CAA-2.

Send notice in CAA-3, with the scheme, explanatory statement and other disclosures, to the Central Government, income tax authorities, RBI, SEBI, the Registrar, Official Liquidator and Competition Commission of India.

The chairman appointed by the NCLT presides. Quorum is as the NCLT fixes. Public shareholders of a listed company vote by postal ballot or e-voting under SEBI rules. A scrutinizer appointed by the NCLT reports to the chairman. The chairman reports the result to the NCLT in CAA-4 within the time fixed, or within 3 days of the meeting if none is fixed.
If members or creditors approve the scheme, with or without changes, file the petition in CAA-5 for sanction under sections 230 and 232.
steps.time: Within 7 days of the certified order or chairman's report

steps.d: The NCLT fixes the hearing date and orders a newspaper notice at least 10 days before it. Publish the notice (Form NCLT-3A as cited), put it on the website, and file an affidavit of compliance at least 3 days before the hearing.
steps.time: 10 days before hearing; affidavit 3 days before

steps.d: Send first and second motion papers and notices to all authorities. The ROC reports to the Regional Director. Reply to queries from the Regional Director and Official Liquidator. Their reports go to the NCLT.
If satisfied, the NCLT sanctions the scheme by an order in CAA-7. File a certified copy with the ROC within 30 days of receiving it, or the time the NCLT fixes.

Board meeting notes the order and fixes a record date. Where shares go to members of a demerged company, a board meeting of the resulting company allots them. File INC-28 within 30 days (section 232(5)). File PAS-3 and SH-7. Make any name, conversion, consolidation, reclassification or reduction changes. Send share certificates or credit demat accounts.

Apply to the stock exchange for listing within 30 days of the sanction order. Before trading starts, advertise in one Hindi and one English national newspaper and one regional paper where the registered office is. Finish trading formalities within 45 days of the order.

Until the scheme is fully carried out, file a statement in CAA-8 each year showing whether the scheme is followed as ordered. A chartered accountant, cost accountant or company secretary in practice must certify it.

forms.purpose: Filing of board resolution and special resolutions

forms.deadline: Time fixed by NCLT, else 3 days

forms.purpose: Order sanctioning the scheme (issued by NCLT)
Filing of NCLT order with ROC

forms.deadline: Within 30 days of allotment as per rules

checklist: Registered valuer appointed and valuation report ready
Draft scheme and explanatory statement settled
Board approval of exchange ratio and scheme
Audit Committee and Independent Directors reports (listed)
Stock exchange filings and website uploads done
Consent affidavits and creditor certificate from CA
Sanction order filed in INC-28 within 30 days

meetings.title: First board meeting to approve the merger proposal
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter with consent of directors)

meetings.title: Second board meeting to approve the scheme
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter with consent of directors)

meetings.title: Meeting of members convened by the NCLT
Board meeting after the sanction order
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter with consent of directors)

resolutions.title: In-principle approval and appointments
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT in-principle approval be and is hereby given to the proposal for merger/amalgamation of [name of transferor company] with {co} under sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013, subject to approvals of members, creditors and the NCLT. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the application be filed before the NCLT, [city] bench, and [name of registered valuer] be appointed as registered valuer. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [names of professionals] be appointed to advise on the scheme, and [name of director] is authorised to settle their terms. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the next board meeting be held on [date] at [time] at [venue].

resolutions.title: Approval of the scheme and exchange ratio
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, on the recommendation of the Audit Committee and after considering the valuation report of [name of valuer] dated [date], the share exchange ratio of [ratio] be and is hereby approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Scheme of [merger/amalgamation] between [name of company] and {co} be approved and a copy be filed with the Registrar of Companies under section 232(2)(b). RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director], [designation], be authorised to sign all documents, make representations before the NCLT, and enter appearances. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT a copy of this resolution be filed in Form MGT-14 within 30 days, as required under sections 117(3)(g) and 179(3)(i).

resolutions.title: Taking note of the sanction order
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the order dated [date] of the NCLT sanctioning the Scheme be taken on record and a certified copy be filed with the Registrar of Companies in Form INC-28 within 30 days of its receipt under section 232(5). RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [date] be fixed as the record date for allotment of shares under the Scheme. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT a board meeting of the resulting company be held on [date] to allot shares to eligible members.

resolutions.title: Approval of the scheme at the meeting convened by the NCLT
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the Scheme of [merger/amalgamation] between [name of company] and {co}, a copy of which is placed before this meeting and initialled by the Chairman for identification, be and is hereby approved under sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013, with such modifications as the NCLT may direct. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to do all acts needed to give effect to the Scheme.
resolutions.explanatory: Statement under section 230(3) to be sent with the notice: terms of the scheme, share exchange ratio and valuation, effect on shareholders, creditors, directors and key managerial personnel, interests of directors, and effect on employees. Approval needs a majority in number of those present and voting, holding three-fourths in value (section 230(6)); it is not a usual special resolution.

docs.title: Intimation to the stock exchange of the board decision
paras: To, [name of stock exchange], [address]. Sub: Outcome of board meeting held on [date] - Scheme of [merger/amalgamation] - {co}.

We inform you that the Board of {co}, at its meeting held on [date] from [time] to [time], approved the Scheme of [merger/amalgamation] of [name of company] with {co}, together with the share exchange ratio of [ratio]. The valuation report, Audit Committee report and fairness opinion are enclosed.

docs.title: Consent affidavit of shareholder or creditor
paras: I, [name], son/daughter of [name], residing at [address], being a [shareholder/secured creditor/unsecured creditor] of {co} holding [number of shares / debt of Rs. amount], solemnly affirm and state as follows.

I have read the draft Scheme of [merger/amalgamation] between [name of company] and {co} and I give my consent to it. I understand this affidavit will be filed before the NCLT in support of the request to dispense with the meeting.

flags: The reference note quotes a Form NCLT-3A for the hearing notice under NCLT Rules. Under the 2016 Rules the advertisement of notice of the petition is in Form CAA-6; check the current form before filing.

The reference note does not mention that statutory authorities get 30 days after receiving notice to give objections (section 230(5)), or that the notice of the meeting is normally one clear month (Rule 6). Verify.

The reference note says notice goes to the Central Government, tax, RBI, SEBI and others but does not name stock exchanges and sectoral regulators; I believe section 230(5) also covers them where relevant.
The reference note describes a demerger share allotment in the post-sanction step; for a plain merger, the transferee company allots shares to the transferor's members. Adjust as needed.

Small company or holding-subsidiary mergers may use fast-track under section 233 (not covered in the reference note). Listed companies must also follow the current SEBI master circular on schemes and the observation letter from the exchange, which the reference note only partly describes.

Section 232(3) conditions such as the 90% creditors' dispensation and the unlisted company exception are as cited in the reference note; confirm against the latest rules because the NCLT sometimes asks for meetings regardless.

title: SME IPO: step-by-step roadmap to listing
law: Sections 2(52), 23, 26, 32, 42, 62, 63, 92, 129, 134, 137, 149, 152, 173, 177 and Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013; SEBI (ICDR) Regulations; SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015
summary: Takes a company from readiness checks through advisers, restructuring, due diligence, filings, marketing, issue and post-listing compliance on an SME platform.
when: When a company plans a public issue and listing on the SME platform of NSE or BSE.
applies: Public limited companies (a private company must convert first)

steps.d: Test why the company needs the IPO and whether the business can scale. Confirm promoters accept dilution, lock-in and compliance duties. Check SME platform eligibility (net worth, tangible assets, profit or alternate route). Clean up shareholding. Review the board and find gaps such as an independent director. Take views of key shareholders and lenders. Meet several SEBI-registered merchant bankers.
Hold a board meeting to approve the IPO proposal and appoint the merchant banker and other advisers.

Appoint the merchant banker (lead manager), legal advisers on both sides, a peer-reviewed auditor for restated financials, a registrar to the issue, a company secretary or compliance consultant, and optionally an internal auditor, ERP consultant or IPO adviser. Start the search for an independent director if none is appointed. Align timelines for due diligence, DRHP and filings.

Convert the private company to a public company, which is a must. Increase authorised capital and file SH-7. Amend the memorandum and articles, inserting Table F-aligned clauses. File MGT-14, INC-27 and SH-7 as needed. Update PAN, GST, UDYAM and other licences. Review or end shareholder agreements that clash with ICDR and LODR. Adopt an ESOP scheme if planned. Disclose beneficial owners. Dematerialise all shares and get the ISIN before DRHP. Keep at least 3 directors. Define promoters and promoter group.

Identify, disclose and regularise related party transactions under sections 2(76) and 188, at arm's length and with the needed approvals. Update statutory registers, share certificates and minutes under the secretarial standards. Make sure individual shareholders have KYC and PAN-Aadhaar linking.

Carry out legal, financial (3 to 5 years of restated statements audited by a peer-reviewed CA), corporate, and business due diligence. Check FEMA/FDI filings (FC-GPR, FC-TRS), labour law, Factories Act, ESOP, internal controls, ERP and IEPF transfers. Adopt a litigation materiality policy. Obtain NOCs from bankers, charge holders, IP owners, landlords, group entities and sector regulators.

Bring annual filings (MGT-7, AOC-4) up to date. File event-based forms: PAS-3, MGT-14, DIR-12, SH-7. File all IPO-related resolutions with the ROC. Check registers (SH-2, SH-6, MBP-2). File PAS-4 and PAS-5 with valuation reports for any pre-IPO private placement. Confirm every director has an active DIN and valid DSC. Complete FEMA filings. Get approvals from RBI, SEBI, IRDAI or other sector regulators where needed.

steps.t: Prepare for SEBI and the exchange
steps.d: Get a valuation report where foreign investors or pre-IPO allotments need it. Finalise the ESOP policy. Move trademarks and IP from promoters or group entities to the company. Sign agreements with depositories, RTA, escrow banks and public issue bankers. Choose NSE Emerge or BSE SME. Settle objects of the issue and risk factors. The merchant banker drafts the DRHP.

steps.t: File the DRHP and get approvals
steps.d: File the DRHP through the merchant banker. The reference note says this goes to SEBI only if the issue exceeds Rs. 10 crore. Answer observations. Apply for in-principle approval of the SME platform. Appoint a monitoring agency if the issue exceeds Rs. 100 crore. Activate ISIN and demat connectivity before opening.

Prepare the investor deck, teaser and FAQ. Run soft pre-marketing without projections or selective disclosure. Train promoters on investor communication. Hold non-deal roadshows. Update the website investor section. Approach anchor investors if used. Keep all media and marketing within SEBI advertising rules and have them pre-approved.
docs: Marketing materials approved by merchant banker

steps.d: Fix the price with the merchant banker and open the issue for at least 3 working days. Have escrow and ASBA ready. Monitor bids. If oversubscribed, allot proportionately. Finalise the basis of allotment with the registrar, merchant banker and exchange. Credit shares to demat accounts and refund excess or unsuccessful amounts. Get final listing and trading approval.
steps.time: Issue open at least 3 working days

steps.d: Follow SME-platform LODR rules (results, board meetings, shareholding patterns). Keep a market maker active for 3 years. Adopt codes of conduct, insider trading and whistleblower policies. Disclose material events under Regulation 30. File the shareholding pattern within 21 days of quarter-end (Regulation 31). Resolve complaints on SCORES. Hold AGMs and file reports. Track and report use of IPO funds.
steps.time: Shareholding pattern within 21 days of each quarter-end

resolutions.title: Approval of the IPO and appointment of advisers
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the proposal of {co} to make an initial public offer of up to [number] equity shares and list them on the SME platform of [NSE Emerge / BSE SME] be and is hereby approved, subject to approval of members and regulators. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of merchant banker], a SEBI-registered merchant banker, be appointed lead manager, and [names] be appointed as legal adviser, peer-reviewed auditor and registrar to the issue. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [names of directors] be authorised to sign engagement letters and agreements for the issue.

resolutions.title: Approval of the draft red herring prospectus
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the Draft Red Herring Prospectus of {co} prepared by [name of merchant banker], including the objects of the issue and the restated financial statements for [financial years], be and is hereby approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Draft Red Herring Prospectus be filed with [the stock exchange / SEBI] through the merchant banker and [name of director] be authorised to make changes in response to observations.

resolutions.title: Conversion into a public company and alteration of MOA and AOA
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under section 18 of the Companies Act, 2013, {co} be converted from a private company into a public company and the word 'Private' be deleted from its name, subject to approval of the Registrar of Companies. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Memorandum of Association be altered as per the draft placed before the meeting and the Articles of Association be replaced by new Articles containing provisions of a public company in line with Table F and listing norms. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to file Form INC-27 and Form MGT-14 and do all things needed.
resolutions.explanatory: The company must be a public company to list on the SME platform. The alteration of the Memorandum and Articles brings them in line with the Companies Act, 2013 for public companies and with SEBI listing norms. Directors may be interested only as members. Copies of the draft Memorandum and Articles are open for inspection at the registered office.

resolutions.title: Increase in authorised share capital
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under section 61 of the Companies Act, 2013, the authorised share capital of {co} be increased from Rs. [existing amount] divided into [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each to Rs. [new amount] divided into [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT clause V of the Memorandum of Association be altered accordingly and Form SH-7 be filed with the Registrar.

resolutions.title: Approval of the public issue of equity shares
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under section 62(1)(c) and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and the SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, the issue and offer of up to [number] equity shares of face value Rs. [amount] each to the public through an initial public offer be and is hereby approved at a price fixed by the Board with the merchant banker. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be authorised to finalise the objects, price band, basis of allotment, and to do all acts needed to complete the issue and listing.
resolutions.explanatory: The proceeds will be used for the objects set out in the draft offer document: [objects]. The issue will list the shares on the SME platform. No director is interested except as a shareholder or to the extent of any shares they subscribe.

resolutions.title: Adoption of an employee stock option scheme (if planned)
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under section 62(1)(b) of the Companies Act, 2013 and applicable SEBI rules, the [name] Employee Stock Option Scheme of {co} be adopted, with up to [number] options each convertible into one equity share of Rs. [face value]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board or its committee be authorised to grant options and settle the terms within the scheme.
resolutions.explanatory: The scheme gives eligible employees the right to apply for shares. Details of the scheme, eligibility, vesting, exercise price and number of options are as in the draft scheme open for inspection at the registered office.

flags: The reference note says Section 2(52) 'excludes SME-listed companies from LODR'. Section 2(52) only defines 'listed company'; exemptions come from SEBI LODR (Regulation 15) and ICDR Chapter IX.
The reference note describes Section 32 as punishment for fraudulently inducing investors. I believe that is section 36; section 32 deals with global depository receipts.

The reference note says the DRHP goes to SEBI only if issue size exceeds Rs. 10 crore. I believe for SME issues the draft offer document is filed with the SME exchange and a copy goes to SEBI; the exact rule should be checked in the current ICDR Chapter IX.
The reference note speaks of quarterly results for SME-listed companies. I believe SME platform companies file half-yearly results; check the current rule.
The reference note gives 3 to 5 years of restated financials; I believe the track record test for SME listing is 3 years with the further conditions of the exchange. Verify.
Procedural steps are drawn on practice and a disclaimer in the reference note says they are indicative. Check current SEBI circulars, exchange eligibility norms and thresholds before acting.

title: Voluntary liquidation of a company
law: Section 59, Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016; IBBI (Voluntary Liquidation Process) Regulations, 2017
summary: Closes a solvent company by a declaration of solvency, special resolution, creditor approval where needed, and a liquidator who sells assets, pays stakeholders and seeks dissolution from the NCLT.
when: When a company with no insolvency wants to wind up on its own and end its existence.
applies: All companies; those with no immovable assets and no outstanding creditors get some relaxations

steps.d: Directors pass a resolution for voluntary liquidation and for calling a members' meeting.

Directors sign the declaration. Attach audited financial statements for the two preceding financial years, a registered valuer's report of the assets (if any is made), and details of pending proceedings, assessments and litigation.
File the declaration of solvency with the Registrar in e-form GNL-2.
Pass two special resolutions: approve the voluntary liquidation and appoint an insolvency professional as liquidator.
If the company owes any debt, get approval from creditors holding two-thirds of the value of the debt.
The liquidator publishes the announcement in Form A in two newspapers with wide circulation, one English and one in the regional language of the registered office area, and informs the IBBI.
The liquidator notifies the ROC in MGT-14 and informs IBBI of the resolution.

Creditors submit their claims. The liquidator opens an account in a scheduled bank in the company's name followed by 'in voluntary liquidation' to receive dues and pay costs. The liquidator then prepares a list of stakeholders from accepted claims.
The liquidator gives the company a preliminary report.
The liquidator arranges deregistration of all licences and registrations.
Sell the assets, deduct liquidation costs, and distribute the balance among stakeholders.
The liquidator completes the process and submits the final report to the ROC in GNL-2 and to the IBBI.
steps.time: The reference note says 90 days, or up to 270 days if claims are received

steps.d: If the process runs beyond the allowed period, the liquidator holds a meeting of contributories.
steps.time: Within 15 days after the period ends

steps.d: The liquidator applies to the NCLT for dissolution. After hearing and being satisfied, the NCLT orders dissolution. File the order with the ROC in GNL-2.

forms.purpose: Declaration of solvency, final report and dissolution order filing
forms.deadline: Declaration with ROC; order within 14 days of the NCLT order

checklist: Directors agree on the solvency declaration
Audited financials for the last 2 years
Valuer's report on assets, if any
List of pending cases and assessments
Creditors holding 2/3 in value approve (if debt exists)
Newspaper announcement in English and regional language
NCLT dissolution order filed with ROC

meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter with consent of directors)

meetings.title: General meeting for voluntary liquidation
meetings.notice_days: At least 21 clear days (shorter with consent of 95% of members)

resolutions.title: Approval of liquidation and declaration of solvency
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under section 59 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, the voluntary liquidation of {co} be and is hereby approved, the company having no debt or being able to pay its debts in full from the proceeds of its assets. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Declaration of Solvency, with audited financial statements for [two financial years], the valuer's report and details of pending proceedings, be approved and signed by the majority of directors. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT a general meeting be called on [date] at [time] at [venue] to seek members' approval, and [name of director] be authorised to file Form GNL-2.

resolutions.title: Special resolution for voluntary liquidation
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under section 59 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, {co} be wound up voluntarily and its voluntary liquidation process commence on [date]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Declaration of Solvency dated [date] placed before the meeting be and is hereby taken on record. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to file Form MGT-14 and other documents.
resolutions.explanatory: The company has no debt or can pay its debts in full within the period stated in the declaration of solvency. A copy of the declaration, audited financial statements and valuer's report are open for inspection at the registered office.

resolutions.title: Appointment of the liquidator
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT [name], an insolvency professional registered with the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (registration no. [number]), be and is hereby appointed liquidator of {co} on a fee of Rs. [amount]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the liquidator be authorised to carry out the voluntary liquidation process under the Code and the IBBI (Voluntary Liquidation Process) Regulations, 2017.
resolutions.explanatory: The liquidator will realise assets, pay stakeholders and apply for dissolution. His written consent and declaration of independence are open for inspection at the registered office.

docs.title: Declaration of solvency
paras: We, the undersigned, being a majority of the directors of {co} (CIN [CIN]), declare that we have made a full inquiry into the affairs of the company and have formed the opinion that the company has no debt, or that it will be able to pay its debts in full from the proceeds of its assets within [period not exceeding 12 months] from the start of voluntary liquidation.

We also declare that the company is not being wound up to defraud any person. Attached are the audited financial statements for [two financial years], the valuation report of [name of valuer] (if any) and a statement of pending proceedings and litigation.
Signed at [place] on [date]: [name and DIN of directors].

flags: The reference note says the liquidator must finish in 90 days (270 days if claims are received). I believe the Regulations allow 12 months from commencement; verify the current rule before using the timeline.

The reference note does not give the 4-week limit for the special resolution after the declaration of solvency, or the 7-day limit for creditors' approval after the resolution (section 59(3)). Confirm both.

The reference note does not say when the public announcement and claims windows run. I believe the announcement is made within 5 days of appointment and claims are due within 30 days of commencement; verify.
The reference note says the final report goes to the ROC in GNL-2. I believe the final report goes to the NCLT with the dissolution application and a copy goes to the Board; verify.
The directors' declaration should state that the company has no debt or can pay in full, and that it is not being wound up to defraud anyone. The reference note omits this.

The reference note's 'exemption' for companies without immovable assets and creditors is unclear: it lists the valuation report and creditor approval, which are only needed where assets and debts exist.

title: Issuing i-SAFE notes to investors
law: Sections 42, 55, 62, 73, 117 and 179, Companies Act, 2013; Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014; Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules, 2014; Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014; Articles of Association; terms of the i-SAFE agreement
summary: A start-up takes investor money under an i-SAFE note that converts into shares later, with board and member approvals and allotment on conversion.
when: When a start-up private company wants to raise early funds through a simple agreement for future equity.
applies: Private limited companies registered as start-ups with DPIIT

steps.d: Confirm the company is a private limited company, the Articles allow the issue, authorised capital is enough, start-up registration with DPIIT is in place, the investor (Indian or foreign) and amount are known, and terms such as lock-in, funding rounds, and premium or discount are final before drafting the agreement.
Gather the incorporation certificate with the memorandum and articles, the start-up registration certificate, and investor identity and address proof with email and mobile numbers.

Approve the issue of i-SAFE notes. Settle the terms of the agreement and authorise directors to sign the agreement and note, subject to members' approval. Approve the notice of the EGM for a special resolution.

Print the agreement on stamp paper and have it notarised (the reference note notes this is not required by the Act). At least two directors and the investor sign every page, and two witnesses sign the last page.
Pass a special resolution for the issue under sections 62 and 117(3)(a) and (b). File MGT-14 within 30 days of the resolution.
After members approve, give the investor the i-SAFE note signed by the directors and witnesses.
Before shares are allotted on conversion, a registered valuer values them.
Board approves allotment against the note. This may happen after the lock-in ends, at the next funding round, or as the agreement says.
File the return of allotment with the Registrar.
Issue share certificates and pay stamp duty.
Enter the allottee in the Register of Members.

checklist: Agreement stamped and signed by 2 directors and witnesses
Valuation by registered valuer before allotment

[amount] on the terms of the i-SAFE agreement placed before the Board be approved, subject to approval of members by special resolution. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [names of two directors] be authorised to sign the i-SAFE agreement and the note on behalf of the company. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT an extraordinary general meeting be held on [date] at [time] at [venue], and the draft notice with the explanatory statement be approved.

resolutions.title: Special resolution for issue of i-SAFE notes
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under sections 42 and 62 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, the issue of i-SAFE notes for Rs. [amount] to [name of investor], convertible into equity shares of {co} on the terms of the i-SAFE agreement dated [date], be and is hereby approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be authorised to allot shares on conversion and to do all things needed, including filing Forms MGT-14 and PAS-3.
resolutions.explanatory: The company proposes to raise Rs. [amount] from [name of investor] under an i-SAFE agreement. The note converts into equity shares at the time of the next funding round, after the lock-in of [period], or as the agreement says, at the valuation or discount stated in it. Shares will be valued by a registered valuer before allotment. No director is interested in the resolution except [name], to the extent of [interest].

resolutions.title: Allotment of shares on conversion of the note
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, based on the valuation report of [name of registered valuer] dated [date], [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each at a premium of Rs. [amount] be allotted to [name of investor] against conversion of the i-SAFE note dated [date]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the share certificate be issued within two months, the Register of Members updated, and Form PAS-3 filed within 15 days of allotment.

flags: The reference note says no forms for approval of issue need to be filed for private companies, but also says to file MGT-14 for the special resolution. A private company must still file MGT-14 for special resolutions; I believe the first statement is wrong or means only board resolutions.

Section 42 usually needs a private placement offer letter (PAS-4), record of offers (PAS-5) and a bank account for the money. The reference note does not mention them; check whether the instrument is treated as shares, debt or deposit.
If the investor is a foreign person, FEMA rules and reporting on convertible notes for start-ups apply. The reference note mentions only that the investor is checked as Indian or foreign.
The reference note cites section 73 (deposits) and 55 (preference shares) with no explanation; confirm how the note is classified before settling the structure.

title: Converting a One Person Company into a private company
law: Section 18, Companies Act, 2013; Rule 6, Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014
summary: An OPC becomes a private limited company by adding members and directors, altering its memorandum and articles, passing special resolutions and filing INC-6.
when: When an OPC wants to take more members and become a regular private company. After the 2021 amendment this is voluntary and has no turnover or capital limit.

steps.d: Send notice at least 7 days before the meeting with the agenda: appoint an additional director, approve conversion in principle, fix the date, time and day of the EGM, approve the draft EGM notice, authorise a director to issue it, approve the draft altered memorandum and articles, and approve the proposed share transfer that increases the members.
Before the EGM, obtain written no-objection from creditors (the reference note also mentions shareholders).
docs: NOC from shareholders (as in the reference note)

steps.d: Send notice to all members, directors and auditors at least 21 days before the EGM, or as the Articles require.

Check quorum is present throughout. Check the auditor attends or has leave of absence under section 146. Pass a special resolution for conversion of the OPC to a private company. Pass a special resolution to alter the memorandum and articles.
File DIR-12 for the additional director, MGT-14 for the special resolutions, and INC-6 for conversion with the creditors' and members' NOC and the other documents prescribed.
The Central Processing Centre reviews the papers. If in order, the ROC issues a certificate of incorporation recording the conversion. The new status starts from the date on the certificate.
Issue new share certificates, update the statutory registers, inform authorities and agencies about the conversion, and change the name if wanted with ROC approval.

forms.purpose: Application for conversion of OPC into a private company
forms.deadline: After the EGM, with prescribed attachments

checklist: At least two members after the share transfer
At least two directors including the existing one
EGM notice to members, directors and auditors, 21 days ahead

meetings.title: Board meeting to approve the conversion
Extraordinary general meeting
meetings.notice_days: At least 21 days (or as per Articles)

resolutions.title: Appointment of additional director
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under section 161 of the Companies Act, 2013, [name], holding DIN [number], be appointed additional director of {co} with effect from [date], to hold office until the next annual general meeting. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT his consent in Form DIR-2 and declaration under section 164 be taken on record.

resolutions.title: In-principle approval and EGM arrangements
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT in-principle approval be given to convert {co} from a One Person Company into a private limited company under section 18 of the Companies Act, 2013. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the draft altered Memorandum and Articles of Association be approved and the proposed transfer of [number] shares from [name] to [name] to raise the number of members to at least two be noted. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT an extraordinary general meeting be held on [date] at [time] at [venue], the draft notice be approved, and [name of director] be authorised to issue it.

resolutions.title: Conversion into a private limited company
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under section 18 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with Rule 6 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014, {co} be converted from a One Person Company into a private limited company, and the words '(OPC)' be removed from its name. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to file Form INC-6 and other forms with the Registrar and do all acts needed.
resolutions.explanatory: The company has [number] members and [number] directors, as required for a private company. Creditors have given no-objection in writing. The conversion has no turnover or capital limit.

resolutions.title: Alteration of Memorandum and Articles
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under sections 13 and 14 of the Companies Act, 2013, the Memorandum of Association be altered to change the name and type of company, and the Articles of Association be altered by adopting the new Articles containing provisions for a private company, as placed before the meeting. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to file Form MGT-14 and make changes the Registrar requires.
resolutions.explanatory: The alteration reflects the change of company type and name, and adds provisions applicable to private companies. Copies of the altered documents are open for inspection at the registered office.

flags: The reference note says the NOC shows no objection to conversion 'into a One Person Company'; this is a slip, since the conversion is out of an OPC.
The reference note asks for no-objection from creditors in the introduction but from shareholders and creditors in step 2; I believe Rule 6 requires creditors' consent. Verify.
The reference note says Board notice goes to 'members'; I believe it goes to directors.

An OPC has one member, so check whether a general meeting is needed or members' decisions can be recorded in the minutes book under section 122; the reference note assumes an EGM after the share transfer.
The reference note does not give the INC-6 timeline or fee. Check the current rule and the attachments needed.

title: Moving a company between active and dormant status
law: Section 455, Companies Act, 2013; Rules 3 and 8, Companies (Miscellaneous) Rules, 2014
summary: A company can apply to be recorded as dormant, and later apply to return to active status, through MSC forms.
when: When a company has no significant activity and wants dormant status, or a dormant company wants to start again.

steps.d: Directors approve the proposal and authorise a director to apply for dormant status.
Pass a special resolution at a general meeting, or get written consent from members holding at least three-fourths in value.
File MSC-1 with a certified copy of the special resolution, a statement of affairs, an auditor's certificate and the lenders' consent.
The ROC checks eligibility, pending compliances and any defaults.
The ROC issues MSC-2 granting dormant status.
To return to active status, the board approves the conversion and authorises a director to apply.
File MSC-4 with the board resolution, a statement of affairs and an auditor's certificate.

steps.t: ROC verifies and grants active status
steps.d: The ROC verifies compliance and clearance of dues, then issues MSC-5 granting active status.

forms.purpose: Certificate of dormant status (issued by ROC)
Certificate of active status (issued by ROC)

checklist: No pending defaults or compliance gaps
Board resolution for return to active status

meetings.title: Board meeting to apply for dormant status
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter with consent of directors)

meetings.title: General meeting for dormant status
meetings.notice_days: At least 21 clear days (shorter with consent of 95% of members)

meetings.title: Board meeting to return to active status
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter with consent of directors)

resolutions.title: Approval to apply for dormant status
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT {co} be made a dormant company under section 455 of the Companies Act, 2013, subject to approval of members and the Registrar. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the statement of affairs as at [date] be approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to file Form MSC-1 and obtain the auditor's certificate and lenders' consent.

resolutions.title: Special resolution for dormant status
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under section 455 of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rule 3 of the Companies (Miscellaneous) Rules, 2014, approval be given to make {co} a dormant company, and to apply to the Registrar of Companies in Form MSC-1. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to do all things needed.
resolutions.explanatory: The company was formed for [purpose] and has had no significant accounting transaction since [date]. Becoming dormant keeps the company on the register while it has no activity. A copy of the statement of affairs is open for inspection at the registered office.

resolutions.title: Approval to become active again
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT {co}, now a dormant company, be converted back to active status and application be made to the Registrar of Companies in Form MSC-4. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the statement of affairs as at [date] be approved and the auditor's certificate be obtained. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to sign and file the form and the attachments.

flags: The reference note omits the eligibility test in section 455: a company formed for a future project or to hold an asset or intellectual property, or one with no significant accounting transaction in the last two financial years. Check it before applying.

The reference note cites Rules 3 and 8; I believe the application for dormant status is Rule 3 and the return to active status is a later rule, and that Rule 8 deals with another matter. Check rule numbers.
The attachments to MSC-1 in the reference note (auditor's certificate, lenders' consent) should be matched with Rule 3 and the form instructions.
The reference note does not mention the yearly MSC-3 return that a dormant company files.

title: Declaration for commencement of business
law: Section 10A, Companies Act, 2013; Rule 23A, Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014
summary: A newly incorporated company with share capital must file a declaration that subscribers have paid for their shares before it starts business or borrows.
when: For a company incorporated after the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2019 that has share capital.
applies: All companies with share capital incorporated after the amendment (private companies are not exempt)

steps.d: A company with share capital incorporated after the 2019 amendment cannot start business or use borrowing powers until the declaration is filed and its registered office is verified.

If the registered office was not given at incorporation, file INC-22 before filing for commencement. Attach proof of the office: registered title document, or a notarised lease or rent agreement in the company's name with a rent receipt not older than one month, and the owner's or occupant's authorisation with proof of ownership. Add a utility bill (phone, gas or electricity) not older than two months. Add photographs of the building and the interior showing at least one director or KMP, with DSC on the form.
docs: Title document or lease and rent receipt

steps.d: Make sure subscribers have paid the amount stated in the subscriber clause of the memorandum into the company's bank account.
The board approves the commencement of business and the filing.

A director's declaration under section 10A goes in e-form INC-20A with the MCA, within 180 days of incorporation. A practising company secretary, chartered accountant or cost accountant must verify and certify it.
docs: Bank statement as proof of capital

steps.d: If the company's work is regulated by RBI, SEBI, IRDAI or another sector regulator, attach its registration or approval to the declaration.

forms.purpose: Notice of situation of registered office
forms.deadline: Before INC-20A if not given at incorporation

checklist: Share capital received in the bank as per subscriber clause
Utility bill not older than two months
Rent receipt not older than one month (if leased)
Photographs with a director or KMP

meetings.title: Board meeting to approve commencement of business
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter with consent of directors)

resolutions.title: Approval of declaration for commencement of business
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under section 10A of the Companies Act, 2013, the Board notes that the subscribers to the Memorandum have paid Rs. [amount] towards the shares agreed in the Memorandum into the bank account of {co} at [bank, branch]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to sign the declaration and file Form INC-20A with the Registrar within 180 days of incorporation, with certification by [name of professional], and to file Form INC-22 if the registered office is yet to be verified. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the company commence business on filing of the declaration.

docs.title: Authorisation from owner for use of premises as registered office
paras: I, [name of owner], owner of the premises at [address], give my consent for {co} to use the premises as its registered office from [date] [free of charge / on rent of Rs. amount per month].
Proof of ownership, namely [title deed / property tax receipt], and a recent [electricity/telephone/gas] bill are attached.

flags: The reference note names the form 'e-Form 20A'; the form is INC-20A.
The reference note step 1 breaks off after 'unless'. Section 10A requires filing the declaration within 180 days and verifying the registered office within 30 days of incorporation.
I believe the section also carries a penalty and a risk of strike off for non-filing; the reference note does not mention it. Verify.
The reference note says the 2019 amendment; the Act took effect with retrospective date of 2 November 2018. Verify the date for older companies.
The reference note's ownership-proof wording is unclear (rent receipt, authorisation, utility bill belong to the owner or occupant); check INC-22 instructions.

title: Shifting the registered office within the same city
law: Section 12, Companies Act, 2013 read with Rules 25 and 27, Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014; Regulations 30 and 46(3), SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 (listed entities)
summary: A company moves its registered office within the local limits of the city by board resolution and files INC-22 with the Registrar.
when: When the registered office moves to a new address in the same city, town or village.
applies: All companies; SEBI steps only for listed companies

steps.d: Hold a board meeting, or pass a resolution by circulation, to approve the change of registered office within local limits and authorise the CS, CFO or any director to file the notice with the ROC.
Tell the stock exchanges within 24 hours of the board meeting and post it on the company website within 2 working days.

File notice of the change with verification, plus fee. Attach a certified copy of the board resolution. If the company owns or leases the office, attach proof of address (conveyance, lease or rent agreement with receipts, and a standard NOC for leased property) and one utility bill not older than 2 months. If the office is owned by a director or another person, attach the same plus proof the company may use the address. Attach photographs of the building and the interior with a director or KMP, and the name board.
steps.time: The reference note says within 30 days of the change

steps.t: Update the address and name board
steps.d: Show the new address outside every office or place of business and on all business letters, bill heads, letter paper, notices and official publications. Fix a name board with the details required by section 12 outside the new registered office.
Tell all statutory authorities where the company is registered about the new address.

forms.purpose: Notice of change in situation of registered office
forms.deadline: The reference note says 30 days from the change

checklist: Proof of address for new office
Utility bill not older than 2 months
Photographs with director or KMP and name board
New address on stationery and signboards

meetings.title: Board meeting or circular resolution to shift the registered office
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter with consent of directors) for a meeting

resolutions.title: Shifting of registered office within local limits
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under section 12 of the Companies Act, 2013, the registered office of {co} be shifted from [old address] to [new address], within the local limits of [city], with effect from [date]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name], [Company Secretary / CFO / Director], be authorised to file Form INC-22 with the Registrar of Companies, attach the documents needed, and pay the fee. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the new address be shown outside every office and on all business letters, bill heads and publications, and a name board be fixed at the new registered office.

flags: The reference note says INC-22 is due within 30 days of the change. I believe section 12(4) requires notice within 15 days of the date of change (30 days applies to the first notice after incorporation). Verify.

The reference note gives no step for the shareholders; a shift within the same city and the same ROC jurisdiction needs a board resolution only. A change of address to a place under a different ROC or state needs different procedure.
Listed companies should check the board-outcome timelines in Regulation 30 and the website placement under Regulation 46.
